data.body:
Parked 2026-10-18 pending two operator inputs, surfaced to the operator in-session:

1. Download approval for `pandoc-3.9-arm64-macOS.zip` from the official jgm/pandoc 3.9 GitHub release (about 30 MB, to `~/.local/pandoc-3.9`), which is the only way to test whether a real arm64 pandoc produces byte-identical conversion outputs to the frozen fixture. Agents cannot approve binary downloads.
2. The fingerprint design choice from the prior comment: (a) accept both the Intel and the arm64 fingerprint under `darwin-arm64` (needs the byte check from item 1), (b) record `darwin-arm64` as the Intel build and drop the byte-identical guarantee there, or (c) remove the `darwin-arm64` entry and check only `linux-x86_64`, which is what CI runs.

Established this session on an arm64 Mac with no Rosetta: the `pypandoc-binary` 1.17 "arm64" wheel ships an x86_64 pandoc whose sha256 matches the pinned `darwin-arm64` value exactly; with no other pandoc present the ticket's named test SKIPS rather than fails; the 17 `Bad CPU type in executable` failures seen in `make verify` by two independent sessions today are the missing arm64 pandoc 3.9 install that `docs/local-dev-env.md` already prescribes, not this fingerprint. Installing that pandoc fixes the 17 and then turns this test red as an 18th. AC1 as written (pin only the arm64 fingerprint) would break every default install, so the description must be rewritten around whichever option is chosen before review. Unclaimed; no code changed.
